clue.text: Such youngsters always come to a fishy end!

definitions.text: Such youngsters always come to a fishy end!

parts.words: Such youngsters always come to a fishy end!
parts.note: children of the sea folk end in a fish tail, so their ends are literally fishy rather than shady

explanation.surface: A grim warning that certain young people are bound to end up in dodgy dealings.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring of mermaids and mermen, who are half fish below the waist.

clue.text: European man holding up place

indicators.note: the word for man holds another piece inside it, like a container

parts.note: a man is a male

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the piece is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to place is to set

explanation.surface: A European fellow is delaying a location.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses the word for place, and 'holding' means the man contains it; 'place' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Malta, a Mediterranean island nation in Europe.

clue.text: Decorate the church in the French way

indicators.note: the abbreviation for church goes inside the French word for a street

parts.note: rue is French for street or way

explanation.surface: Someone adorns the parish church with a Gallic flourish.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim fabric or a garment with gathered frills, a pleated ornamental edging.

clue.text: Sheds rain, showing sturdy quality

indicators.note: the letters of the first two words are put on show in a new order

explanation.surface: A waterproof coat that sheds rain proves it is tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Toughness or robustness, the capacity to endure hard conditions.

clue.text: Instrument to steal, from the sound of it

indicators.note: the word for stealing is said out loud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to loot is to steal, especially in riots or war

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a musical instrument is worth pinching, judging by its tone.
explanation.definitionFit: A plucked stringed musical instrument with a pear-shaped body, popular in Renaissance Europe.

clue.text: The leftist ended in confusion and blushed

parts.note: a red is a communist or left-winger

indicators.note: the letters of the word ended are muddled up into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A left-wing politician's speech finished chaotically and he turned pink with embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The leftist' is the usual crossword red, and 'in confusion' scrambles the word ended that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Turned red in the face, as when flushing with embarrassment.

clue.text: A loop the egghead promptly sent back

indicators.note: both pieces together are returned, read from end to start

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of the word egg
soon means without delay, promptly

explanation.surface: An intellectual quickly returned a ring of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop with a running knot that tightens when pulled, as on a lasso.

clue.text: Time, the !" Byron (Childe Harold)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing word completes a line from Byron's long poem Childe Harold's Pilgrimage

explanation.surface: A quotation from Byron's poem Childe Harold with its last word left blank.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed blank stands for the missing word of Byron's line, which calls time one who exacts revenge.
explanation.definitionFit: Byron's line personifies time as one who takes revenge for wrongs done.

clue.text: All object about serving men

indicators.note: the word for an object goes round, or about, the abbreviation for soldiers

parts.note: an entity is a thing or object
RE is the Royal Engineers, men serving in the British Army

explanation.surface: Everything objects to the treatment of servants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving men' is the common crossword shorthand for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps; 'about' puts them inside the word for an object.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole of something, every part taken together.

clue.text: Hurt when one in fifty complained

indicators.note: the word for one is placed inside the letters for fifty and complained

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
to rate someone is to scold or complain at them
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: One person in fifty grumbled about being harmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rate' is an old verb meaning to scold angrily.
explanation.definitionFit: Wounded by tearing or cutting, as with torn flesh or gashed skin.

clue.text: A beast of a light-weight

definitions.meaning: a snow leopard, a big cat of Central Asian mountains
a small unit of weight, one sixteenth of a pound

explanation.definitionFit: It names both the snow leopard and a small imperial unit of weight, about 28 grams.

clue.text: Protection for the viewer

parts.note: the viewer is not a spectator but the organ of sight itself, shielded by a fold of skin

explanation.surface: Something to shield the people watching a show.
explanation.definitionFit: The fold of skin that closes over and protects the eye.

clue.text: Separating, so girl's returning ring

indicators.note: the girl's name with its possessive is read backwards

parts.note: Eve's, the possessive of the girl's name Eve
taken as written

explanation.surface: Breaking up, so the girl gives back the engagement ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns EVES into SEVE, followed by RING.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting off or dividing, breaking a connection.

clue.text: Removed deer, as destructive

indicators.note: the letters of deer and as are destroyed and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A deer was taken away because it was damaging things.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiped out or deleted, rubbed away.

clue.text: This bean is used to make an alcoholic drink

indicators.note: the letters of the first two words are used to make a different word

explanation.surface: A particular bean goes into making a strong spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is used to make' rearranges THIS BEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong green spirit flavoured with wormwood and anise.

clue.text: Come again and gather some fruit

parts.note: to reap is to gather in a harvest
a pear is a kind of fruit

explanation.surface: An invitation to return and pick the fruit harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: To show up once more after vanishing.

clue.text: Ship's officer taking in tea for the person who's paid for it

definitions.text: the person who's paid for it

indicators.note: the ship's officer takes the word for tea inside him

parts.note: a purser is the officer handling a ship's accounts
cha is an informal British word for tea

explanation.surface: A ship's officer drinking tea for whoever settled the bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A buyer, someone who has bought something.

clue.text: A supporter lacking in discipline

indicators.note: the last word is missing the little word that precedes it

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fan whose team has poor discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower or adherent of a teacher or cause.

clue.text: A criminal needing a ship to get dope in

parts.note: SS is short for steamship
an ass is a fool or dope
taken as written

explanation.surface: A villain requiring a boat to smuggle drugs in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' looks like drugs but means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A killer who murders for money or politics, the gravest kind of lawbreaker.

clue.text: Join a number going to a Mediterranean island

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
Crete is the largest Greek island

explanation.surface: Someone joins a crowd travelling to a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow together or attach by gradual accumulation.

clue.text: Draw and learn about fish

indicators.note: the word for learn goes round the fish

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: An instruction to sketch and study marine life.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw with a waxy coloured stick, as children do.

clue.text: One horse in twelve is in such shape

indicators.note: the horse is placed inside the word for twelve o'clock

parts.note: noon is twelve o'clock midday
a nag is a horse, usually old or poor

explanation.surface: A single horse among twelve is in this condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane figure with nine sides and nine angles.

clue.text: Make a reduction and it's a bar gain!

definitions.meaning: the split word is a bargain, a formal agreement or deal

explanation.definitionFit: To shrink, and also a binding agreement such as a bargain struck between parties.

clue.text: Some place where mites can relax

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used

explanation.surface: A spot where tiny bugs can take it easy.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sense meaning to slacken or ease off.

clue.text: He cons constituents when elected

indicators.note: the letters of the first two words are the parts used to build something new

explanation.surface: A politician fools the voters in his seat once he wins office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' is not voters here; it rearranges HE CONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Picked or selected, as by vote.

clue.text: A Canadian river worker

definitions.meaning: the river that flows from Alberta into Great ... Lake

explanation.definitionFit: It names a river in northern Canada and also a drudge forced to toil.

clue.text: Enclosures for birds

explanation.definitionFit: Livestock enclosures, and female swans.

clue.text: Notes taken by a radio operator in Surrey

parts.note: E and G are musical notes
a ham is an amateur radio operator

explanation.surface: A radio enthusiast in the Home Counties jots down some notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in that English county, near Runnymede on the Thames; Surrey is a county south-west of London.

clue.text: A bunch of reporters keen to enlist help?

parts.note: the press is reporters collectively
a gang is a group or bunch

explanation.surface: A crowd of journalists eager to get assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: A press gang forcibly enlisted men for the Royal Navy in the 18th century.
explanation.definitionFit: A squad that forcibly recruited sailors, hence one keen to sign up helpers.

clue.text: Terse characters drive on to see a certain specialist

indicators.note: the letters, or characters, of the first word are mixed into a new order

parts.note: an urge is a drive or impulse
taken as written

explanation.surface: Curt words push someone on to consult an expert.
explanation.definitionFit: An arborist, an expert who tends and repairs damaged woodland plants.
